grid.fixture_note: this is the published grid DECIMATED — every 20th row and column, so a cell holds one real 0.25° cell's month rather than a 5° average. The arithmetic a consumer does is identical; the picture is sparser.
grid.index_rule: iy = clip(floor((lat + 90) / 5.0), 0, 36), ix = clip(floor((lon + 180) / 5.0), 0, 71), on the row's CELL CENTRE

read_rule: one month of BOTH channels is one contiguous range: offset = header_len + i * slab_bytes, length = slab_bytes, where i is the index of the month in `months`. The response must be HTTP 206; a 200 means the host ignored the Range and is sending the whole file.
recipe_cmd: python3 ml/build_family10_stores.py --store fishing --work <dir> --stage all   # the store and this grid; then python3 ml/publish_fishing_index.py

source.citation: Global Fishing Watch (2025). Global AIS-based Apparent Fishing Effort Dataset, version 3.0 [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14982712
source.known_issues: E-081 §1 records the source's own known issues verbatim: 2024 is provisional; AIS reception is uneven in space and time, so absence of effort is NOT absence of fishing; an MMSI is not always one vessel (spoofing, reflagging, recycling); and one gear class is assigned per MMSI over the whole record.
source.name: Global Fishing Watch — Global AIS-based Apparent Fishing Effort Dataset
source.table: mmsi-daily-csvs-10-v3-<year>.zip — one row per (day, 0.1° cell, MMSI)

qc_codes.0: unknown — the vessel table has no row for this MMSI in this year
qc_codes.meaning: the vessel's GEAR CLASS (vessel_class_gfw in the source's vessel table), NOT a quality grade

totals.note: the grid's per-month sums were asserted equal to the store's at build time, in float64, to better than 1e-3 relative — the difference is float16 rounding per cell

zero_is_a_value: 0 means no vessel broadcast in that cell that month, and is stored as 0 — not NaN. The grid has no missing values at all.
